headline: Intel's worst day since 1974 drags tech lower, Claude drops the 5-hour cap on its $200 plan, and Google runs Gemma in orbit

stories.title: Intel heads for its worst day since 1974 and drags tech down, as the AI spending bill spooks investors
facts: Intel shares fell as much as 30% on Friday after its results, on pace for the worst day since 1974 (this morning's after-hours drop was 21%).
CNBC says the slide wipes about $12bn off the US government's Intel stake; Reuters says it set off a global chip rout.
The Nasdaq sank more than 3.5% and opened at its lowest level in more than two months; Amazon and Reddit also fell, the BBC reports.
Alphabet slipped about 1% more in early trading after losing more than $500bn on Thursday, when AI search summaries were blamed for weaker search ad revenue.
The BBC adds that Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon and Microsoft are committing $800.6bn to AI spending in 2026, with Alphabet's investment spending rising to as much as $205bn.
stories.whyItMatters: After a week of big-tech earnings, the market is now punishing heavy AI spending and any sign that AI eats into existing businesses, not just weak results.

image.alt: BBC News graphic for the tech share selloff

stories.title: Anthropic renames Claude's top plans to Max and Ultra and drops the 5-hour limit for Ultra
facts: Max 5x becomes Max and Max 20x becomes Ultra; prices stay at $100 and $200 a month and subscribers don't need to do anything.
The 5-hour usage limit goes away for verified Ultra accounts, starting today for most existing subscribers.
Newer accounts keep a temporary limit until they're verified, which Anthropic calls a fraud and abuse measure; they get an email when it lifts.
Weekly limits are unchanged. Claude Code lead Boris Cherny confirmed the change on X.
stories.whyItMatters: For heavy Claude Code users, the 5-hour window was the cap they hit most; now the weekly limit is the only ceiling on the $200 plan.

image.alt: Claude announcement image for the Max and Ultra plans

stories.title: Google's Project Suncatcher satellite ran Gemma 4 in orbit and sent back a haiku
facts: Google calls it the first AI response from a data-centre-class TPU in orbit: during a ground-station pass it uplinked a prompt, and the answer came down over Svalbard.
The model was the open Gemma 4; the poem read "Blue marble below / Data streams in silent grace / Starlight feeds my core."
The prototype launched on Oct 1, and commissioning took about three weeks, TechCrunch reports.
It carries four TPUs but generates only up to 1 kW, so a TPU can run for about 20 minutes at a time.
Next come thermal-stress and radiation tests, then a pair of interconnected satellites.

stories.title: Four days before the US midterms, Cook moves 12 more House races toward Democrats
facts: Cook Political Report shifted a dozen more House races toward Democrats and says they could win up to 240 seats on Tuesday, which the Washington Post calls their biggest majority since 2009.
Trump reversed course and will hold the weekend rallies in Iowa and Kansas he had cancelled, with Senate control at stake (NBC, AP, Reuters).
Pope Leo XIV sent in his mail-in ballot, making him the first pope to vote in a US election, CNN reports.

stories.title: Breach day: Northflank tells users to rotate every secret, hackers steal Charité data, and AO3 stays dark
facts: Northflank says all users should assume their environment variables were decrypted and rotate them now; Wiz flagged the threat at 11:43 UTC and patches followed through the afternoon.
Northflank says several users confirmed their AI API keys were used; it enabled secret rotation for Postgres and MongoDB addons and advises turning off public exposure on addons.
Berlin's Charité says attackers took data on patients and staff from a web server; the cause is unclear and those affected will be told (ZEIT, rbb).

Fan-fiction archive AO3 has been offline since Oct 29 after a security incident, may need up to four weeks to come back, and urges password changes, though it doesn't believe its user database was taken.
Separately, GitHub had its second outage of the day, with Webhooks, Actions and Pages degraded.
stories.whyItMatters: If you deploy anything on Northflank, rotate keys tonight; the confirmed misuse of AI keys means this isn't theoretical.

facts.text: Bloomberg via IGN: EA chose Star Wars Battlefront 3 over Mass Effect 5 under the $18bn debt from its $55bn Saudi-led buyout; about 400 EA jobs (3%) go, BioWare's Austin studio stays open.
German inflation fell to 2.8% in October, helped by the fuel discount (Tankrabatt).
"Gen Z regelt" youth protests are planned on Saturday in Mainz, Hamburg, Baden-Württemberg and other cities; organisers and police say they want them peaceful.
Russia is evacuating Oleshky in occupied Kherson region, MDR and ZEIT report.
At the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Wadephul refused a family photo with Lavrov, and there won't be one.
A Houston ICE officer was indicted on a felony after allegedly hitting a man with his vehicle.
The NYT says the US is sending dozens of Afghans detained in Louisiana back to Afghanistan despite the risk of persecution.
Proton's CEO cancelled the AI-led staff "re-interviews" after a 404 Media investigation.
NASA asked industry for ideas on commercially servicing the Hubble Space Telescope.

GitHub Agentic Workflows is generally available: workflows written in Markdown compile to Actions YAML, run read-only by default in a sandbox behind a firewall, and work on Free, Team and Enterprise (the Copilot CLI engine needs a Copilot licence).
OpenAI launched Private Intelligence for businesses.
Google's Antigravity agent is coming to Android Studio.
Vercel folded its Data Cache into Runtime Cache with no code changes for Next.js fetch or unstable_cache, and Pro and Enterprise get more storage.
Vercel also released Geist Serif, a high-contrast display serif for the Geist family.
Vercel's fx v0.0.16 cuts uncached input tokens by 41% and npm downloads of libfx by about 60%.
Guillermo Rauch teased "Next Native" as coming.
Three.js r187 is out.
Playwright merged a change that serves every WebSocket-enabled server under a random path.
Worth reading: how curl was accidentally Turing-complete for nine months.
Eintracht Braunschweig were 0:2 down at half-time at Arminia Bielefeld.
Bayern host Dortmund on Saturday; Bayern are again without Neuer and Kimmich's return is open, Absolut Fussball reports.
The Warriors play the Lakers tonight, and both teams could be missing a starter, Sports Illustrated says.
Basketball Löwen Braunschweig's next home game is against defensively strong Würzburg.
